summary.whatChanges: Converts the npm release workflow from push-triggered to manual dispatch only, drops the version-change detection job, and gates publishing behind a reviewer-approved `npm` GitHub environment. The `mini_version` input becomes optional and selects back-publish vs. normal release. AGENTS.md and the security-advisory skill are updated to match.
behaviorChanges: Pushing a version bump (or any change to packages/*/package.json or the workflow file) to main no longer triggers a release; nothing publishes on push.
Releases now require a manual `workflow_dispatch` run that pauses for approval in the `npm` environment before publishing.
The `mini_version` dispatch input is now optional; empty means a normal release, a value means back-publishing @zod/mini only.
Test, lint and circular-dependency jobs run only on the normal-release path (empty `mini_version`), not on back-publish dispatches.
The version_changed job and its guard are gone, so a dispatch runs the publish path regardless of whether a version was bumped.
risks: With version-change detection removed, a dispatch without a bump relies solely on each publish step skipping already-published versions; if any step lacks that guard it could fail or republish.

Releases now depend on a manually configured `npm` environment (reviewers, branch restriction, trusted publisher binding) that is not visible in the diff; misconfiguration would either block or over-permit publishing.
Back-publish dispatches skip test, lint and circular-dependency gates entirely.
Documentation hardcodes a specific environment ID and reviewer names, which can drift from the actual GitHub settings.
